name: Maya by Kulissa
summary: Voice role-play for sales training: learners talk through a practice call with an AI virtual customer, an AI coach steps in when they go wrong, and the session is scored with quotes from the transcript. Runs in the browser with a microphone. In beta.

value: Spoken practice calls with an AI virtual customer
Live coaching that pauses the call and suggests a better approach
Browser and microphone only, nothing to install

value.notes: A free three-minute public demo; no team pricing published.

Privacy policy is written for the GDPR and the Swiss FADP. The app and database run on Hetzner; AI processing is by US providers (OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs, via OpenRouter for some requests). Several processing locations are marked 'to be confirmed'.
Providers named on the subprocessor page, without model versions. Kulissa says it doesn't train its own models on customer content and requires providers not to.

answers.question: Trains AI models on customer data
answers.value: No: Kulissa says it doesn't train its own models on customer content and requires providers not to

answers.question: How long prompts and chats are kept
answers.value: Demo transcripts up to 90 days; session traces 7 days; customer data for the life of the contract, then deleted or returned within 30 days
answers.note: Backup retention 'to be confirmed'. Live audio is not kept beyond transcription unless the customer sets longer retention.

answers.question: Who processes the data
answers.value: Hetzner (hosting), Cloudflare, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, ElevenLabs and others listed by name
answers.note: AI providers process in the US; several locations 'to be confirmed'.

answers.question: AI models used
answers.value: OpenAI and Google Gemini language models, ElevenLabs speech, and Anthropic models via OpenRouter; versions not named

answers.question: Minimum learner age
answers.note: Privacy policy: does not knowingly collect data from anyone under 16; described as a B2B product for adults at work.

answers.question: Staff can review AI output before learners see it
Staff can set limits on the AI
How it responds to learners
answers.value: Coaches: the coach pauses the call when the learner goes wrong, shows a better approach, and the learner tries again

answers.question: Answers from your own course content
Who owns what the AI produces
answers.value: Customer: playbooks and recordings belong to the customer; transcripts and scores stay under the customer's control

researchTasks: Submitted at /submit on 12 Nov 2026 by Fernando Leyra, CEO, under video-interactive; moved to ai-for-learning (AI voice role-play with AI scoring), with video-interactive as secondary. Jim emailed questions on 14 Nov 2026.

Submission claims (not yet on a page we've opened): upload your own playbooks, ICP and evaluation criteria; the same buyer and rubric for every job applicant; English, French and German tuned for sales practice. The site footer shows English only. Confirm each on a public page or record it as vendor-supplied from Fernando's reply.
Test it: the free three-minute demo is public, and the submission says a free trial covers reviewer access. Product video: https://youtu.be/dR1t7_wX3Vs.

Privacy policy mentions 'recordings' as customer product data in Roles and the FAQ, but the retention table says live audio isn't kept beyond transcription. Ask which is right before setting retention above vendor-disclosed.
Ask: can staff see learners' sessions and scores; can admins restrict scenarios or the AI's behaviour; does the AI use the customer's uploaded playbooks, and does feedback cite them?
Ask: team pricing and pricing basis; geographic availability; accessibility conformance; any security certification.
Find comparable products for alternatives once other AI role-play tools are in the directory.

dataGaps.note: No team pricing published; only a free public demo.
None listed apart from Google and Microsoft sign-in.
No conformance report or standard published.
Hetzner server locations partly 'to be confirmed'; AI processing in the US.
